summary: Frontend-only verification of AuthContext.logout defensive tweak (captures token BEFORE clearing localStorage and passes it as explicit Authorization: Bearer header to fire-and-forget POST /api/auth/logout). All 3 acceptance criteria PASS. Confirmed via network interception that the background POST /api/auth/logout now carries Authorization: Bearer <token> header (belt+suspenders alongside httpOnly cookie). Logout UI redirect measured at 258ms. JTI revocation confirmed: GET /api/auth/me with the pre-logout localStorage token returns 401 {"detail":"Sesión revocada"} after ~4s. No regressions: back button stays on /login (auth guard active), re-login works, and /clientes /prestamos /caja protected pages load correctly after re-login.
action_items: None — ship as-is. The prior code review concern from iteration_5 (fire-and-forget logout losing Authorization header because token was removed before axios request built) is now resolved by explicit Bearer header injection.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext.jsx L35-47: correct order — capture oldToken, clear localStorage, setUser(false), fire POST with explicit Bearer header, then window.location.replace('/login'). Verified in browser network trace: request URL /api/auth/logout, method POST, header 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...' present.

The explicit cfg = { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${oldToken}` } } bypasses the axios request interceptor's localStorage read (which would return null since we already cleared it). Good defensive coding.

Verified backend revocation: POST /auth/logout with Bearer header successfully revokes JTI → old token returns 401 'Sesión revocada' on subsequent /auth/me. Works even in cross-origin scenarios where cookie might not traverse.
context_for_next_testing_agent: AuthContext.logout now sends BOTH the httpOnly cookie (via credentials:'include') AND an explicit Authorization: Bearer header captured before localStorage clear. If the token variable is captured from a direct API login before the UI login, it will represent a DIFFERENT JTI than what the UI is using — always read the token from localStorage AFTER UI login to correctly test JTI revocation. Iteration_5 concern is resolved.
rca_of_the_issue: Prior state (iteration_5): logout was fire-and-forget with immediate redirect, revocation worked but relied solely on httpOnly cookie because localStorage token was removed BEFORE axios request built its headers. Tweak in this iteration: capture token first, then remove it, then pass explicit Authorization header in the axios call config. Verified via network interception (Authorization: Bearer <jwt> present on POST /api/auth/logout) and via /auth/me returning 401 'Sesión revocada' with the pre-logout token.
